c.tagline: Baroque old town wrapped in green hills

emergency.note: 112 covers police, fire and ambulance, and English-speaking operators are generally available.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Senamiestis (Old Town): Vilnius Cathedral and Gediminas Tower on Castle Hill
hood_landmark.Uzupis: the Užupis Angel statue of the self-declared artists' republic
hood_landmark.Naujamiestis: the Daniel Libeskind-designed MO modern art museum
hood_landmark.Zverynas: century-old wooden villas and the green-domed Orthodox Church of the Sign
hood_landmark.Antakalnis: St Peter and St Paul's Church with its 2,000 stucco figures

avoid.reason: Watch drinks and inflated bar tabs in Old Town nightlife and keep usual awareness around the train station area late at night.

hood_desc: One of Europe's largest baroque old towns, with cobbled streets, churches, cafes and the cathedral; suits first-time visitors wanting atmosphere and walkable sights.
A quirky, bohemian self-declared republic across the river, with artist studios, galleries and offbeat bars; suits creatives and travelers wanting character and a laid-back vibe.
The emerging hip district around the station and business center, with restaurants, startups and the Paupys development; suits younger travelers wanting a modern, up-and-coming base near transport.
A leafy residential riverside district of wooden villas and quiet streets just west of the center; suits those wanting a calm, green, authentic neighborhood within easy reach of the center.
A historic residential district northeast along the river with parks, hilltop views and the Antakalnis cemetery; suits longer-stay visitors wanting a tranquil local setting.
lodging: Courtyard by Marriott Vilnius City Center
Karolina Park Hotel and Conference Centre

water.note: Tap water is safe and among the cleanest in Europe.

transit.pay: Tap a contactless bank card directly on the validator (cheapest option), buy an m-ticket through the JUDU/Trafi app, or get a rechargeable Vilniečio kortelė card at Narvesen kiosks and top it up. A single ride is about €1 via card/app versus about €2 paid in cash to the driver.
transit.hours: Buses and trolleybuses run roughly 5am-midnight, with limited night routes on weekends.

transit.m: Airport train to Vilnius station, ~8 min

food.name: Cepelinai
food.desc: Zeppelin-shaped grated-potato dumplings stuffed with minced pork or curd, blanketed in bacon-and-sour-cream sauce - Lithuania's heavyweight national dish.

places.name: Bernelių Užeiga
places.note: Rustic folk-styled dining rooms; a mini-cepelinai sampler platter lets you try several fillings at once.

places.name: Etno Dvaras
places.note: Cellar restaurant on the main tourist street with the full canon of Lithuanian classics and English menus.

places.name: Žemaičių Ąsotis
places.note: Local pub a short walk out of Old Town; huge portions at prices locals actually pay.

food.name: Šaltibarščiai
food.desc: Shocking-pink chilled beetroot and kefir soup with dill, cucumber and egg, served with a plate of hot boiled potatoes - the summer staple.

places.name: Etno Dvaras
places.note: Served year-round, not just in summer, with the traditional side of hot potatoes.

places.name: Bernelių Užeiga
places.note: Generous bowl with plenty of dill and egg; reliable partner to a plate of cepelinai.

places.name: Gabi
places.note: Small Old Town kitchen locals rate for homestyle versions of both saltibarsciai and cepelinai.

food.name: Kibinai
food.desc: Crescent pastries of the Karaim community near Trakai, filled with chopped lamb and onion and baked until the crust flakes - eaten with clear broth.

places.name: Senoji Kibininė
places.note: The best-known kibinai name in Lithuania, with city branches as well as the original Trakai lakeside shop.

places.name: Kybynlar
places.note: Karaim family restaurant; lamb, mushroom and curd kibinai baked to order, worth the day trip to Trakai.

places.name: Etno Dvaras
places.note: Convenient central option if you are not making it out to Trakai.

food.name: Kepta duona
food.desc: Sticks of dark rye bread fried in oil, rubbed with raw garlic and showered in cheese - the beer snack every Lithuanian pub puts on the table.

places.name: Stikliai Aludė
places.note: Lively historic cellar tavern; the classic place for garlic rye bread with a jug of poured beer.

places.name: Šnekutis
places.note: Scruffy, much-loved beer bar chain pouring farmhouse ales with proper pub snacks.

places.name: Bernelių Užeiga
places.note: Tidy sit-down version alongside the rest of the traditional menu.

food.name: Bulviniai blynai and vedarai
food.desc: Crisp grated-potato pancakes with sour cream, and vedarai - potato sausage baked in intestine casing and served with bacon crackling.

places.name: Žemaičių Ąsotis
places.note: Old-school Lithuanian pub food in big portions; vedarai and potato pancakes both done well.

places.name: Senoji Trobelė
places.note: Country-cottage styled dining room with a slightly more refined take on the potato repertoire.

places.name: Etno Dvaras
places.note: Potato pancakes with mushroom sauce or sour cream, easy to order in English.

food.name: Šakotis
food.desc: Spiky golden tree cake, batter drizzled onto a rotating spit over open flame until it grows branches - the celebration cake of Lithuania.

places.name: Halės Turgus (Halle Market)
places.note: Market bakers sell šakotis by the slice or whole ring, alongside smoked meats and dark rye.

places.name: Pilies gatve craft stalls
places.note: Outdoor stalls on the main street sell boxed šakotis and honey cake as takeaway souvenirs.

places.name: Bernelių Užeiga
places.note: Keeps šakotis and other traditional sweets on the dessert menu with coffee.

food.name: Gira
food.desc: Lightly fermented rye-bread kvass, faintly sweet and barely alcoholic, poured from the tap all over Lithuania - the everyday soft drink.

places.name: Šnekutis
places.note: Homemade gira alongside the farmhouse beers; ask for the unfiltered version.

places.name: Etno Dvaras
places.note: House gira served in ceramic jugs with the traditional food.

places.name: Halės Turgus (Halle Market)
places.note: Market stalls sell bottled gira to take away, often flavoured with berries.

food.name: Lithuanian farmhouse beer and midus
food.desc: Kaimiskas country ales brewed with open fermentation and native yeasts, plus midus, the spiced honey mead revived by small Lithuanian producers.

places.name: Šnekutis
places.note: The reference point for kaimiskas beer in Vilnius; unfussy rooms, rotating village breweries.

places.name: Alaus Biblioteka
places.note: Beer Library pours a broad Lithuanian craft and farmhouse selection with knowledgeable staff.

places.name: Bambalynė
places.note: Bottle-shop cellar with hundreds of Lithuanian beers and meads to drink in or take away.

landmarks: Vilnius Cathedral & Bell Tower
The neoclassical white cathedral and its freestanding bell tower anchor Cathedral Square, Vilnius's most iconic and symmetrical photo spot.
Gediminas' Tower
A red-brick medieval tower atop a hill overlooking the Old Town, offering the definitive panoramic view of Vilnius.
Vilnius University
One of Europe's oldest universities, its Grand Courtyard's arcaded Renaissance architecture is a favorite for atmospheric photography.
St. Anne's Church
A masterpiece of flamboyant Gothic brickwork so admired that Napoleon reportedly wanted to carry it back to Paris.
Užupis
A bohemian, self-declared 'republic' district of cobbled streets, street art, and the whimsical Angel of Užupis statue.
Vilnius Town Hall
A grand neoclassical building anchoring Town Hall Square, the historic and social heart of the Old Town.
Three Crosses Hill
Three white crosses on a hilltop overlooking the Old Town, giving one of the best elevated views and sunset shots of Vilnius.
Gate of Dawn
The last surviving city gate of Vilnius, housing a revered icon chapel and a striking Baroque facade over the old street.
Vilnius TV Tower
A soaring modern tower with an observation deck offering sweeping views far beyond the historic center's rooftops.
Presidential Palace
A stately white neoclassical palace with a formal courtyard, one of the oldest and most photogenic official buildings in the Old Town.

train.note: Trains leave from Vilnius railway station (Geležinkelio g. 16). The international service to Poland involves one quick cross-platform change at Mockava on the Lithuanian border, then continues to Warsaw and Kraków - book the whole journey on LTG Link. Trains to Belarus (Minsk) and Russia are suspended.

bus.note: International coaches use Vilnius Bus Station (Autobusų stotis) at Sodų g. 22, right beside the train station. Frequent buses run to Riga (~4h) and Warsaw. Lithuania, Latvia and Poland are all in the Schengen area, so there are no routine border checks, but carry ID.

intl.to: Kiel (Germany) - departs Klaipeda port, ~4h from Vilnius

ferry.note: Vilnius is inland, so there are no ferries from the city itself. International ferries sail from Klaipeda on the coast (about 4 hours away by train or bus): DFDS runs overnight crossings to Kiel in Germany and Karlshamn in Sweden.

half.name: Kaunas
half.blurb: Lithuania's second city, known for interwar architecture and a lively riverside old town.

half.name: Panevėžys
half.blurb: Lithuanian city known for its parks, theaters, and small-city charm.

full.name: Minsk
full.blurb: Belarus's capital known for its broad Soviet-era boulevards and monumental architecture.

full.name: Riga
full.blurb: Baltic capital known for Art Nouveau architecture and a lively medieval old town.

full.name: Hrodna
full.blurb: Historic Belarusian city near the Polish border, rich in old churches and castles.

full.name: Białystok
full.blurb: Northeastern Polish city known for its baroque palace and multicultural history.

full.name: Baranovichi
full.blurb: Belarusian railway hub city with a modest, industrious small-city character.

full.name: Barysaw
full.blurb: Historic Belarusian town on the Berezina River, site of a famous Napoleonic crossing.

full.name: Šiauliai
full.blurb: Northern Lithuanian city known for industry and its proximity to the famous Hill of Crosses.
